answer.rationale: p99 write-path latency began climbing ~30 minutes after a release shipped 2 hours ago — strong temporal correlation points to the new build as the likely cause. Memory_b1 documents that a rollback cleared a prior checkout error spike with no customer impact; I am verifying it to confirm the archived details match this failure mode before committing. Peak settlement traffic argues against capacity-only or failover gambles: add_capacity is slow to take effect and regional_failover risks write loss during a heavy-write window, violating the no-lost-writes objective. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing address dependency and read load, not write-path latency from a suspect build. Rolling back to the known-stable prior build is the highest-probability fix and preserves writes since the prior schema/build was already handling settlement traffic. If verification of memory_b1 contradicts this (e.g., the prior rollback was for a read-path issue), I would fall back to add_capacity.
